DINESH MATHEW J.MURICKEN  JOHN DANIEL (OLAPPURA)
 THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 07.01.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA No. 2257 of 2014  3  2025:KER:8478  C.PRATHEEP KUMAR, J.

--------------------------------------
 Dated this the 07th day of January, 2025  JUDGMENT

The petitioners in O.P.(MV) No. 719/2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Muvattupuzha are the appellants herein.
The respondents in the O.P. are the respondents herein.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 03.02.2010.
2. During the pendency of the appeal, the appellant died on 16.12.2020.
His mother and brother were impleaded as additional appellants 2 & 3.

sentences.text: According to the petitioner, on 03.2.2010 at about 8 p.m. while he was riding pillion on the motorcycle Reg. No. KL-7 BF 9741 ridden by the 2nd respondent through Kuttampuzha - Thattekkadu public road from east to west, the motorcycle hit against an electric post and as a result, he sustained serious head injuries.
It is alleged that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the 2nd respondent.

The 1st respondent is the owner,
the 2nd respondent is the rider and 3rd respondent is 2025:KER:8478 the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
4. The 1st and 2nd respondents remained ex-parte.
The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documents Exts.A1 to A10, B1 and C1.
6.
After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,93,445/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

9. Heard Smt. Aney Paul, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri. Dinesh Mathew J. Muricken, learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10.
The Point: The fact that the petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident involving motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KL-07/BF 2025:KER:8478 9741 is not disputed.
It is also disputed that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 2nd respondent, who was the rider of the offending motorcycle.

11. The injuries sustained by the petitioner as noted in Ext. A5 wound certificate are the following:
Concious bilateral bleed present.

Lacerated wounds: 1. 5x1cm poor ear pinna 2. 3x1cm Chin (R) hemiparesis Apharic CT Brain - Subarachnoid hemorrhage Subdural hemorrhage and hemorrhage Contusion of brain suggestive of severe head injury

12. Ext. C1 is the disability certificate issued by the medical board constituted by the Superintendent,
Government Medical College, Kottayam in which total permanent whole body disability of the petitioner is fixed at 60%.

In Ext.C1 details of the disabilies are shown as follows:
1. Dysphasia, Forgetfulness, easily getting angry .....15%
2.
Right hemiparesis.
Right grip weakness.
Loss of digital dexterity.....40%
Gaint - stands with support.
Walking on level with occasional support.

Short shuffled gait 3. Risk of PTE not on drugs......5%
13.
From the evidence on record, it appears that in the accident, the petitioner sustained severe head injuries, contusion of brain, Subarachnoid 2025:KER:8478 hemorrhage, Subdural hemorrhage etc.
After the incident he was bed ridden till he breath his last on 16.12.2020.

In the above circumstances, though the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is estimated by the medical board at 60%, his functional disability is to be taken as 100%.
14.
The petitioner was a driver by profession.
It is true that in the claim petition, the monthly income is claimed as Rs.6,000/-, but the tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.3,500/-.

Since the petitioner failed to prove the income as claimed in the claim petition, in order to award just and reasonable compensation, his notional income is liable to be fixed in the light of the dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236].

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the above decision, the notional income of a Coolie during the year 2010 will come to Rs.7,500/-.
15. Since the petitioner was a driver by profession and he has produced his driving licence to prove the same, I hold that his notional income could be fixed at Rs.8,000/-.
Since he was aged 24 at the time of the accident, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects and the multiplier is to be applied is 18.
Therefore, loss of disability will come to Rs.24,19,200/-.
16. Towards the loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.42,000/-.
Since the disability of the petitioner was fixed at 100%, no 2025:KER:8478 further compensation is liable to be awarded under the head loss of earnings.
Therefore, Rs.42,000/- awarded under the head loss of earning is to be deducted.
17. Towards pain and suffering, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.45,000/-.
In this case the petitioner sustained severe head injury on 03.02.2010 and he was bed ridden till he breath is last on 16.12.2020.
That means he was bed ridden on account of the injuries sustained in the accident for a period of 10 years and 10 months.
In the above circumstances, the compensation awarded on pain and suffering is too meagre.
Hence it is enhanced Rs.5,00,000/-.
18. Towards loss of amenities the tribunal has awarded only Rs.35,000/-.

Considering the fact that the petitioner sustained serious injuries and he was bedridden for more 10 years and 10 months, till he breathed his last on 16.12.2020, compensation towards loss of amenities awarded is too meagre *

and it is enhanced Rs.2,00,000/-.
19.
Towards bystander expense the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.8,250/- alone.
Since the petitioner was bed ridden till he breathed his last on 16.12.2020, the petitioner is entitled to get a reasonable compensation towards bystander expense.

In the decision in Kajal v. Jagadeesh Chand &
Others [2020 (4) SCC

Kajal v. Jagadeesh Chand &
Others [2020 (4) SCC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 413],for a child laying in vegetative stage, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has awarded the expense of two bystanders @ Rs.5,000/- each 2025:KER:8478 with a multiplier of 18.
In the instant case I hold that in the absence of any positive evidence, the expense of one bystander @ Rs.5,000/- for the period he was bedridden will be a reasonable compensation.

Therefore,
towards bystander expense, the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.6,50,000/- (5000x130 months).
20.
Towards extra nourishment, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,000/- which is too meagre when compared to the period during which the petitioner was bedridden.
Therefore, the compensation on the head extra nourishment charges is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
21. The petitioner has produced additional bills for Rs.1,32,919/- being medical bills and taxi bills.

Learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent would argue that the total amount in the bills will come to only Rs.1,15,000/-, which is accepted by the learned counsel for the petitioner, at the time of arguments.
Therefore, towards additional medical expense a sum of Rs.1,15,000/- is awarded.
22. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
23. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.39,43,995/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

from the date of the petition till realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
